generated_for: A60 - AI4Mobility: A Multimodal Assistive Platform for Parents Supporting Children with Mobility Difficulties
note: Each programme stores the original source description verbatim in `original_description`. The `steps` array is the output of the step-splitting engine, reviewed against the source. Both are displayed in the interface.

programmes.title: Lower Limb Exercises
programmes.subtitle: General range of movement and strengthening
programmes.goal: General lower limb range of movement and strengthening. Performed lying down, so the programme remains accessible from a bed.
programmes.source_name: Sheffield Children's NHS Foundation Trust — General lower limb exercises
programmes.original_description: Ankle flexion: lay on your back with your leg straight. Point your foot and toes down to the floor or bed, then slowly pull your foot and toes up towards your knee. Repeat 10 times. Quadriceps contraction: lay on your back with your legs outstretched and your foot and toes pointing upward. Push your knee down firmly against the bed and hold for 5 seconds. Repeat 10 times. Glute squeeze: lay on your back with legs outstretched. Squeeze your bottom firmly together, hold for 5 seconds then relax. Repeat 10 times. Knee bending: lay on your back or sit. Bend your knee by bringing your heel towards your bottom, then return to the starting position. Repeat 10 times. Hip abduction: lay on your back with your legs together. Keeping your leg straight, bring your leg out to the side and return to the starting position. Make sure that you keep your knee and foot in line and your toes pointing upwards. Repeat 10 times. Prone lying: lay on your tummy with your head and arms positioned comfortably. Make sure your hips are level and in contact with the bed. Lie for 30 minutes.
programmes.safety: These are general exercises. Follow the specific programme given by your own physiotherapist. Stop and seek advice if pain gets worse.

steps.title: Ankle flexion
steps.text: Lay on your back with your leg straight. Point your foot and toes down to the floor or bed, then slowly pull your foot and toes up towards your knee.

steps.title: Quadriceps contraction
steps.text: With your legs outstretched and toes pointing upward, push your knee down firmly against the bed.

steps.title: Glute squeeze
steps.text: Lay on your back with legs outstretched and squeeze your bottom firmly together, then relax.

steps.title: Knee bending
steps.text: Lay on your back or sit, then bend your knee by bringing your heel towards your bottom and return to the start.

steps.title: Hip abduction
steps.text: Lay on your back with legs together. Keeping your leg straight, bring your leg out to the side and return. Keep your knee and foot in line and your toes pointing upwards.

steps.title: Prone lying
steps.text: Lay on your tummy with your head and arms comfortable and your hips level and in contact with the bed.

programmes.title: Core and Hip Stability
programmes.subtitle: Paediatric physiotherapy programme
programmes.goal: Builds core and hip stability, which underpins balance, walking and the more demanding movements in the other programmes.
programmes.source_name: Sheffield Children's NHS Foundation Trust — Core and hip stability exercises
programmes.original_description: All exercises should be performed 10 times, 3 to 4 times daily throughout the day, and all movements should be slow and smooth. Hip clams: lie on your side with the affected side on top, bend both legs and keep your pelvis level. Slowly lift your top knee away from the bottom knee, keeping feet and ankles together, then lower back down. Bridging: lie on your back with knees bent and feet apart and firmly on the surface. Squeeze your buttocks together and push through your heels, raising your bottom until your hips line up with your knees. Hold for 5 seconds. Four point kneeling: on hands and knees with wrists below shoulders and knees below hips, pull your stomach up and in, then extend one leg straight behind and hold for 5 seconds. Repeat on the opposite leg. One leg stands: stand upright on the affected leg using support if needed, keep your pelvis level and hold for 5 to 10 seconds. Hip hitching: standing upright, keep your pelvis level, lift your hip towards your shoulder and hold for 5 seconds. Dead bug: lie on your back with arms extended straight above and legs bent at right angles, then extend one arm overhead while lowering the opposite leg and return. Four point hip extension: lie on your stomach, bend the affected knee to a right angle and slowly raise your foot towards the ceiling, holding for 5 seconds.
programmes.safety: If pain becomes worse, stop the exercises and seek advice from a healthcare professional. Only perform the movements prescribed for your current stage.

steps.title: Hip clams
steps.text: Lie on your side with both legs bent and your pelvis level. Slowly lift your top knee away from the bottom knee, keeping feet and ankles together, then lower back down.

steps.title: Bridging
steps.text: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet firmly down. Squeeze your buttocks and push through your heels, raising your bottom until your hips line up with your knees.

steps.title: Four point kneeling
steps.text: On hands and knees, pull your stomach up and in, then extend one leg straight behind you. Repeat on the opposite leg.

steps.title: One leg stands
steps.text: Stand upright on one leg, using support if needed, and keep your pelvis level.

steps.title: Hip hitching
steps.text: Standing upright with your pelvis level, lift your hip towards your shoulder.

steps.title: Dead bug
steps.text: Lie on your back with arms straight above and legs bent at right angles. Extend one arm overhead while lowering the opposite leg, then return.

steps.title: Four point hip extension
steps.text: Lie on your stomach, bend your knee to a right angle and slowly raise your foot towards the ceiling.

programmes.title: Glute Strengthening
programmes.subtitle: Progressive hip and buttock strengthening
programmes.goal: Strengthens the gluteal muscles, which control the hip during standing, walking, stairs and single-leg balance.
programmes.source_name: Sheffield Children's NHS Foundation Trust — Glute strengthening
programmes.original_description: Bridge: lie on your back with legs bent and back flattened into the bed. Squeeze your bottom and roll your bottom and back off the floor. Hold for 5 seconds and then lower back down. Control the movement up and down. Repeat 10 to 12 times. Bridge with leg lift: lie on your back with legs bent and back flattened into the bed. Squeeze your glutes and lift your hips off the floor. Straighten one leg and hold for 3 to 5 seconds. Try to keep your hips level whilst you do this. Lower the foot and return to the start. Repeat 6 times on each side. Thigh lift: lie on your front with one knee bent and a pillow under your hips. Lift your thigh off the floor trying to keep your lower back still so the movement is coming from your bottom. Hold for a second and then relax. Repeat 6 times on each side. Clam: lie on your side with knees bent. Lift your top knee while keeping your feet together. Only lift as far as you can control, stop when you feel the top hip starting to roll back. Keep your torso steady. Continue until the side glute muscle is fatigued, then repeat on the other leg. Step up high: stand at a step with your right foot on it. Step up and lift your left leg, pause for balance, then lower the left leg. Repeat on the same side 10 times, then switch so the left foot is on the step. A higher step increases the difficulty. Chair squat: stand in front of a chair or bed. Lower your bottom down, as if you are going to sit on the chair. Just tap your bottom on the chair and then stand back up tall. Avoid using your arms for assistance. Repeat 10 to 12 times.
programmes.safety: If you find the exercises cause you more pain please stop the exercises and seek advice from a healthcare professional.

steps.title: Bridge
steps.text: Lie on your back with legs bent and back flattened down. Squeeze your bottom and roll your bottom and back off the floor, then lower back down with control.

steps.title: Bridge with leg lift
steps.text: Lift your hips off the floor, then straighten one leg while keeping your hips level. Lower the foot and return to the start.

steps.title: Thigh lift
steps.text: Lie on your front with one knee bent and a pillow under your hips. Lift your thigh off the floor, keeping your lower back still so the movement comes from your bottom.

steps.title: Clam
steps.text: Lie on your side with knees bent. Lift your top knee while keeping your feet together. Only lift as far as you can control, and stop when the top hip starts to roll back.

steps.title: Step up high
steps.text: Stand at a step with one foot on it. Step up and lift the other leg, pause for balance, then lower it. Repeat on the same side, then switch.

steps.title: Chair squat
steps.text: Stand in front of a chair. Lower your bottom down as if you are going to sit, tap the chair, then stand back up tall without using your arms.

programmes.title: Calf Control
programmes.subtitle: Gastrocnemius and soleus control
programmes.goal: Builds calf strength and control for walking, stair climbing and balance, targeting both calf muscles separately.
programmes.source_name: Sheffield Children's NHS Foundation Trust — Calf control exercises
programmes.original_description: These exercises should be performed 2 times per day. Gastrocnemius: stand on one leg with your leg straight, holding onto a wall or flat surface for balance. Lift up onto your tip toes, as high as you are able, then slowly lower back down. Repeat as many times as you can. Stop if your muscles feel tired or if you lose control of the movement. Soleus: stand on one leg with your knee bent, holding onto a wall or flat surface for balance. Lift your heel so you are standing on your tip toes, as high as possible, keeping your knee still and bent throughout. Slowly lower back down. Repeat as many times as you can. Stop if your muscles tire or you lose control of the movement.
programmes.safety: Stop if your muscles feel tired or if you lose control of the movement. Always use a wall or flat surface for balance.

steps.title: Gastrocnemius raise
steps.text: Stand on one leg with your leg straight, holding a wall for balance. Lift up onto your tip toes as high as you are able, then slowly lower back down.

steps.title: Soleus raise
steps.text: Stand on one leg with your knee bent, holding a wall for balance. Lift your heel as high as possible, keeping the knee still and bent, then slowly lower.

programmes.title: Wrist and Hand Exercises
programmes.subtitle: Active and assisted wrist movement
programmes.goal: Maintains wrist range of movement and forearm rotation, both actively and with assistance from the other hand.
programmes.source_name: Sheffield Children's NHS Foundation Trust — Wrist exercises
programmes.original_description: Active exercises. Wrist flex: resting your forearm on a table, bring the wrist up and down, trying to bend as far down as you can and bring up as far as you can. Wrist side stretch: move your wrist from side to side. Forearm twist: keep your elbow into your side and turn your palm to face up and face down. Assisted exercises, using your other hand to help. Palm stretch: use your other hand holding the palm to bring back the wrist to feel a stretch. Back of the hand stretch: use your other hand to push down the wrist until you feel a gentle stretch. Prayer wrist stretch: put your hands together as if in prayer to stretch the wrist, keeping your fingers straight. Seated hand pushdown: in a sitting position, place your hands by your side with your fingers pointing behind you and gently push down. Wall push: put your hands flat against a wall and gently push against the wall to feel a stretch.
programmes.safety: Your therapist will fill in how many repetitions to do and how long to hold each stretch. Move gently and stop at the point of a comfortable stretch, not pain.

steps.title: Wrist flex
steps.text: Resting your forearm on a table, bring the wrist up and down, bending as far down as you can and up as far as you can.

steps.title: Wrist side stretch
steps.text: Move your wrist from side to side.

steps.title: Forearm twist
steps.text: Keep your elbow into your side and turn your palm to face up and then face down.

steps.title: Palm stretch
steps.text: Use your other hand, holding the palm, to bring the wrist back until you feel a stretch.

steps.title: Back of the hand stretch
steps.text: Use your other hand to push the wrist down until you feel a gentle stretch.

steps.title: Prayer wrist stretch
steps.text: Put your hands together as if in prayer to stretch the wrist, keeping your fingers straight.

steps.title: Wall push
steps.text: Put your hands flat against a wall and gently push against the wall to feel a stretch.

programmes.title: Child's Pose
programmes.subtitle: Balasana
programmes.goal: Lengthens the lower back and hips and provides a resting position between more demanding exercises.
programmes.source_name: Standard therapeutic resting posture, described from general practice
programmes.original_description: Kneel on the floor with your knees apart and your big toes touching. Sit back onto your heels, then fold forward and rest your tummy between your thighs. Stretch your arms out in front of you along the floor and let your forehead rest down. Breathe slowly and hold the position, then walk your hands back and sit up.
programmes.safety: Stop if there is knee or hip pain. A cushion under the hips or knees makes the position easier to hold.

steps.title: Kneel
steps.text: Kneel on the floor with your knees apart and your big toes touching.

steps.title: Sit back
steps.text: Sit back onto your heels.

steps.title: Fold forward
steps.text: Fold forward and rest your tummy between your thighs.

steps.title: Extend the arms
steps.text: Stretch your arms out in front of you along the floor and let your forehead rest down.

steps.title: Hold
steps.text: Breathe slowly and hold the position.

steps.title: Return
steps.text: Walk your hands back and sit up.

programmes.title: Cat–Cow Stretch
programmes.subtitle: Marjaryasana–Bitilasana
programmes.goal: Moves the spine through flexion and extension to improve back mobility and body awareness.
programmes.source_name: Widely used mobility exercise, described from general practice
programmes.original_description: Start on your hands and knees with your wrists under your shoulders and your knees under your hips. Breathe in and drop your tummy towards the floor, lifting your chest and looking gently forwards. Breathe out and round your back up towards the ceiling, tucking your chin towards your chest. Move slowly between the two positions and repeat ten times.
programmes.safety: Move slowly and only as far as is comfortable. Stop if there is neck or back pain.

steps.title: Four point kneeling
steps.text: Start on your hands and knees with your wrists under your shoulders and your knees under your hips.

steps.title: Cow
steps.text: Breathe in and drop your tummy towards the floor, lifting your chest and looking gently forwards.

steps.title: Cat
steps.text: Breathe out and round your back up towards the ceiling, tucking your chin towards your chest.

steps.title: Flow between the two
steps.text: Move slowly between the two positions.

programmes.title: Thread the Needle
programmes.subtitle: Parsva Balasana
programmes.goal: Stretches the shoulders, arms, upper back and neck, and adds gentle rotation to the upper spine.
programmes.original_description: Start in Table pose on hands and knees, then slide the right hand between the left hand and left knee. Slide the arm all the way out to the left so that the right shoulder and side of the head rest comfortably on the floor. Inhale and reach the left hand up towards the ceiling. Breathe and hold for 3 to 6 breaths. Release by exhaling your palm back down and slowly inhaling to return to Table pose. Repeat on the opposite side.
programmes.safety: Avoid if there is recent or chronic injury to the knees, shoulders or neck. A folded blanket under the knees protects them from pressure.

steps.title: Four point kneeling
steps.text: Start in Table pose on hands and knees.

steps.title: Thread the arm through
steps.text: Slide the right hand between the left hand and left knee.

steps.title: Lower the shoulder
steps.text: Slide the arm all the way out to the left so that the right shoulder and side of the head rest comfortably on the floor.

steps.title: Reach upwards
steps.text: Inhale and reach the left hand up towards the ceiling.

steps.title: Hold
steps.text: Breathe and hold for three to six breaths.

steps.title: Return
steps.text: Exhale your palm back down and slowly inhale to return to Table pose.

steps.title: Repeat on the other side
steps.text: Repeat the sequence on the opposite side.

programmes.title: Standing Balance
programmes.subtitle: Static and dynamic balance practice
programmes.goal: Practises static and moving balance, progressing from a wide base of support to single-leg stance.
programmes.source_name: Standard balance progression, described from general practice
programmes.original_description: Stand tall with your feet together and hold the position, using a support nearby if you need it. Then place one foot directly in front of the other, heel to toe, and hold. Next stand on one leg, keeping your pelvis level, and hold before swapping sides. Finally walk in a straight line placing your heel directly in front of the toes of the other foot each step. Progress each exercise by reducing how much you hold on, and then by closing your eyes if it is safe to do so.
programmes.safety: Always practise beside a wall, worktop or chair. Have someone nearby when trying a harder progression for the first time. Do not close your eyes unless a supervising adult is present.

steps.title: Feet together
steps.text: Stand tall with your feet together and hold the position, using a support nearby if you need it.

steps.title: Heel to toe stand
steps.text: Place one foot directly in front of the other, heel to toe, and hold.

steps.title: Single leg stand
steps.text: Stand on one leg, keeping your pelvis level, then swap sides.

steps.title: Heel to toe walking
steps.text: Walk in a straight line, placing your heel directly in front of the toes of the other foot each step.

programmes.title: Seated Upper Body
programmes.subtitle: Shoulder, neck and trunk mobility
programmes.goal: Maintains shoulder, neck and trunk mobility from a seated position, suitable when standing exercises are not appropriate.
programmes.source_name: Standard seated mobility routine, described from general practice
programmes.original_description: Sit tall in a supportive chair with both feet flat on the floor. Roll your shoulders slowly backwards in a full circle, then forwards. Reach both arms up above your head as far as is comfortable and lower them again. Tilt your head gently towards one shoulder until you feel a stretch along the side of your neck, hold, then repeat on the other side. Finally, with your feet still, turn your shoulders to look behind you on one side, hold, and repeat on the other side.
programmes.safety: Move slowly and keep within a comfortable range. Stop any movement that causes dizziness, pain or pins and needles.

steps.title: Sit tall
steps.text: Sit tall in a supportive chair with both feet flat on the floor.

steps.title: Shoulder rolls
steps.text: Roll your shoulders slowly backwards in a full circle, then forwards.

steps.title: Overhead reach
steps.text: Reach both arms up above your head as far as is comfortable, then lower them again.

steps.title: Neck side stretch
steps.text: Tilt your head gently towards one shoulder until you feel a stretch along the side of your neck, then repeat on the other side.

steps.title: Seated rotation
steps.text: Keeping your feet still, turn your shoulders to look behind you on one side, then repeat on the other side.
